Plots for Glycoverse Data Containers

autoplot.glyexp_experiment.Rd

Visualization for glyexp::GlycomicSE(), glyexp::GlycoproteomicSE(), and other compatible SummarizedExperiment objects. Possible types of plots:

  • "heatmap": (Default) Expression heatmap with columns as samples and rows as variables.

  • "boxplot": Boxplot of expression values for each sample.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'glyexp_experiment'
autoplot(
  object,
  ...,
  type = "heatmap",
  group_col = "group",
  log_transform = NULL,
  scale = "row",
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  row_cluster_tree = TRUE,
  col_cluster_tree = TRUE,
  show_rownames = FALSE,
  show_colnames = NULL,
  na_col = "grey90",
  points = TRUE,
  ncol = NULL,
  label_width = 24,
  scales = "free_y",
  title = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  fontsize = 9,
  family = "sans",
  palette = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
autoplot(
  object,
  ...,
  type = "heatmap",
  group_col = "group",
  log_transform = NULL,
  scale = "row",
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  row_cluster_tree = TRUE,
  col_cluster_tree = TRUE,
  show_rownames = FALSE,
  show_colnames = NULL,
  na_col = "grey90",
  points = TRUE,
  ncol = NULL,
  label_width = 24,
  scales = "free_y",
  title = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  fontsize = 9,
  family = "sans",
  palette = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A supported Glycoverse data container.

...

Must be empty. Supply plotting controls by their full argument names.

type

The type of plot, one of "heatmap" (default) or "boxplot".

group_col

A character string specifying where to find the group information. It should be a column in the sample information tibble. Defaults to "group". Only applicable to "boxplot".

log_transform

NULL (default) uses recorded abundance scale metadata: raw values are transformed with log2(x + 1e-6), while already logged values are unchanged. FALSE always uses the supplied values unchanged. TRUE requests the same transformation for raw values, but warns and is ignored for already logged values. This argument must be named after ....

scale

Standardize rows ("row", the default), columns ("column"), or neither ("none"). Applied after and independently of log_transform.

cluster_rows, cluster_cols

Whether to cluster rows or columns, or compatible hclust objects. Clustering controls the heatmap order.

row_cluster_tree, col_cluster_tree

Whether to display the row or column clustering tree. Both default to TRUE. Hiding a tree preserves clustering order. No tree is drawn when clustering for that axis is disabled or cannot be computed.

show_rownames

Whether to display row labels. Defaults to FALSE.

show_colnames

Whether to display column labels. NULL displays them automatically for at most 40 samples.

na_col

Color for missing values.

points

Whether to show observations as jittered points. Boxes show medians and quartiles with 1.5-IQR whiskers. Outliers are drawn separately only when points = FALSE.

ncol

Number of facet columns. NULL chooses up to three columns.

label_width

Width used to wrap facet labels without truncation.

scales

Facet axis scales, passed to ggplot2::facet_wrap(). Defaults to "free_y"; use "fixed" for comparisons across facets.

title

Optional plot title. Defaults to NULL.

width, height

Plot-area dimensions in millimetres. NULL uses the tidyplots defaults (50 by 50 mm); NA fills the available graphics device. These are not export-page dimensions.

fontsize

Base text size in points. Defaults to 9.

family

Font family. Defaults to "sans".

palette

Color vector. A named vector maps group names to fixed colors across plots and subsets; unnamed palettes follow factor order. NULL selects the plot-specific default: blue-white-red for continuous heatmaps, directional colors for volcano and S-plots, selection colors for ranked dot plots, and distinct hues for other plots.

Value

A tidyplot object, also inheriting from ggplot.

Details

Heatmap options (scale, cluster_rows, cluster_cols, row_cluster_tree, col_cluster_tree, show_rownames, show_colnames, na_col) apply only to type = "heatmap". Boxplot options (points, ncol, label_width, scales) apply only to type = "boxplot".

For SE containers, fortify() returns .sample and .variable axis identifiers and an abundance value column. Ordinary sample and variable metadata are retained. Conflicting annotation names receive numeric suffixes, with sample metadata preceding variable metadata. Boxplot group_col always selects the original column in colData(). Legacy experiment fortification retains sample and variable identifiers.

See also

glyvis_abundance_scale for scale metadata and compatibility rules.
